exposure: Assessment of symptoms of obstetric anal sphincter injuries (OASIs)
Clinical grade of obstetric anal sphincter injuries (OASIs)
outcome: Accuracy of symptom assessment and clinical grade of tear
cohort: The study included 607 women with a history of OASI who were in the second half of a subsequent pregnancy between 2002 and 2022.
finding: Symptom assessment and clinical grade of OASI alone are not sufficient to guide mode of delivery recommendations in a subsequent birth.
mod_finding: Symptom assessment and clinical grade of OASI cannot be used solely to guide mode of delivery recommendations in a subsequent birth, although the absence of symptoms in women with 3a tears has a high negative predictive value, suggesting a vaginal birth can be recommended for these women.
